column1: # GOLDEN reference embeddings (§1) — line format: label<TAB>f0,f1,...  where label is
# "<input-id>|last" (jina-embeddings-v5 uses last-token pooling; the golden covers LAST).
# Produced OFFLINE by scripts/gen-golden.py: the FP32 PyTorch model
# jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano-retrieval loaded via sentence-transformers (torch_dtype=
# float32), encoding each input with prompt_name=role (query/document — the model applies
# its own "Query: "/"Document: " prompt; text is NOT prefixed by hand), L2-normalized,
# dim 768. This is fully independent of the GGUF/llama.cpp path, so the
# parity check is not circular — it directly mirrors the downstream GGUF-vs-PyTorch-FP32
# benchmark that first caught v0.1.151-1.
# Regenerate with scripts/gen-golden.py whenever inputs.tsv, the reference GGUF, or the
# golden model revision (reference-model.env) changes.
# Provenance (filled by gen-golden.py):
#   golden model : jinaai/jina-embeddings-v5-text-nano-retrieval  rev <fill-in>
#   dtype/dim    : float32 / 768,  pooling: last,  normalize: L2
#   prefixes     : query="Query: "  document="Document: "
#   compared to  : v5-nano-retrieval-IQ4_NL.gguf  (threshold cosine >= 0.98, quant vs FP32)
# UNTIL this file has data rows, scripts/correctness.sh treats §1 golden parity as
# "not_generated": it logs a warning and records it in build-info.json, while the §2
# tuned-vs-generic and §4 self-consistency checks remain HARD release gates. Run
# scripts/gen-golden.py and commit the result to activate the golden gate.
